title: I resigned from my life in London to become a goat that lives in the Swiss mountains: Brit created prosthetic legs, ate grass, was accepted by the flock … and says they do "people better than us"
text:
Exhausted by the stress and strains of modern life, Thomas Thwaites decided to give up comfort and try the home if the grass really was greener elsewhere, living as a goat in Switzerland.
The then 35 -year -old from London took his unusual idea so seriously that he spent a whole year creating “prosthetic goat legs for galivantes around the Alps on all fours, as well as an artificial stomach that would allow him to” eat lawn ‘.
And strangely that the concept may seem, the biggest goal for Thomas was “to get out of myself and experiment the world from a different perspective”, even if that meant spending their days chewing grass and avoiding some goats that were less accepting their new friend human.
At the end of his experiment, Thomas discovered that in fact he had become “one of his numbers” and came to find that the mountain inhabitants did “better people than us.”
Speaking to Mailonline, he said: ‘When I had the idea for the first time, many people called me crazy, but I was fed up with my life and needed a break.
‘I was unemployed and I had many personal problems, and I found everyday life so stressful.
“One day I was walking with a friend’s dog and I noticed that the dog seemed very happy for life, without worries, and I thought for myself that it would really be great to be for a day.”
He considered becoming a dog, he explained, but was not interested in eating meat.
Thomas Thwaites decided to give up comfort and try the home if the grass was literally greener, living like a goat in Switzerland
Thomas spent a whole year creating “Prosthetic goat legs” around the Alps on four legs, as well as an artificial stomach that would allow him to “eat grass”
It is not a joke: the biggest goal for Thomas was “to get out of myself and experiment the world from a different perspective”
The adventurous researcher then landed in the idea of ​​becoming an elephant, but then realized that ‘they seem to have the same problems we do: they get sad, they got angry and can even suffer post -traumatic stress.
“That was exactly the kind of things I was trying to get away.”
However, goats offered a seemingly perfect solution to everything he was looking for.
After requested a university subsidy to study goat psychology, Thomas tracked a goat in the town of Wolfenschésen in Switzerland, which was prepared to take it for a few days while the animals grazed in their summer grass.
Then came the challenge of living like a goat, which meant being able to walk on all fours and digest grass.
The researcher requested the help of a prostheses clinic in Manchester to create his ‘goat legs’, while experts from Aberystwyth University designed the ‘stomach’ of a goat for him, which was tied to his waist.
‘I could tie this bag to my torso and a jump chewed the grass in an opening and suck the cultivated microbes and volatile fatty acids of another opening like a shake, to be able to digest them in my real stomach and live in the grass in the Alps as A goat, “he said.
There was inevitably obstacles to life as a goat, which sometimes became a literal uphill struggle.
The researcher requested the help of a prostheses clinic in Manchester to create his ‘goat legs’
There were inevitably obstacles to life like a goat, which sometimes became a literal uphill struggle
He said: ‘I suffered a lot as a goat, due to the slope that I was constantly falling and, of course, I had to eat grass.
‘Also, goats didn’t seem to like them very much, sometimes I thought they were really going to try to attack me. And they have particularly dangerous horns.
“But then I realized that they were only making me know that there was a hierarchy, and I should know my place.”
However, despite the challenges, Thomas thanked his time as a goat.
“I learned something important, and even goats have a difficult life and need to fight for their existence,” he explained.
‘Every day was difficult, and that is something that is part of being alive.
‘The other thing that I think I found is that goats are better people. They live much more at the time we, and show us that we really need to learn to be a little more relaxed about life ‘.
At the end of his experiment, Thomas felt that he had integrated with the flock, and even won a new friend.
At the end of his experiment, Thomas felt that he had integrated with the pack in Switzerland
Thomas is measured by his prostheses before his time living as a goat in the Alps
Thomas said: ‘The best moment was when one of the goats suddenly decided that he was going to be my friend, and that he followed me everywhere.
‘She smells with my nose and I like to close.
“The goat told me in the end that the pack had accepted me as one of its number, it was a great feeling.”
He wrote a best -selling book in 2016 about his adventure: Goatman: how I took a holiday from being a human being, and even received a prize.
Thomas received a Nobel IG Prize, which are granted annually to “honor the achievements that first make people laugh and then make them think.”
